**None of the three proposed solutions is correct.** The correct minimum positive fractional revival time is $t^* = 2\pi/p$.

**Spectrum.** The eigenvalues are Ramanujan sums $c_{2p}(k)=\sum_{d\mid\gcd(2p,k)}\mu(2p/d)\,d$:
- $k=0$: $\lambda = p-1$ (multiplicity 1)
- $k=p$: $\lambda = 1-p$ (multiplicity 1)
- even $k\neq 0$: $\lambda = -1$ (multiplicity $p-1$)
- odd $k\neq p$: $\lambda = 1$ (multiplicity $p-1$)

Check at $p=3$: $X=C_6$, whose spectrum $\{2,1,-1,-2,-1,1\}$ matches.

**Amplitudes.** Writing $U(t)_{x,0}=\frac{1}{2p}\sum_k e^{-it\lambda_k}\omega^{kx}$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/2p}$:
- $\langle 0|U|0\rangle = \dfrac{\cos((p-1)t)+(p-1)\cos t}{p}$
- $\langle p|U|0\rangle = \dfrac{i\,[(p-1)\sin t-\sin((p-1)t)]}{p}$

**Support condition.** For $x\notin\{0,p\}$, the amplitude vanishes for all such $x$ exactly when
$$\cos((p-1)t)=\cos t \quad\text{and}\quad \sin((p-1)t)=-\sin t,$$
which is equivalent to $e^{ipt}=1$, i.e. $t=2\pi m/p$.

At $t=2\pi/p$, $\langle p|U|0\rangle = i\sin(2\pi/p)\neq 0$ and $\langle 0|U|0\rangle=\cos(2\pi/p)$, which has modulus below 1, so the revival is genuinely fractional. The minimum positive time is therefore $t^*=2\pi/p$.

**Evaluating the candidates.**
- **Solution 1** ($2\pi/(p-1)$) correctly finds the spectral radius $p-1$ but wrongly assumes the revival time is set by that single eigenvalue. It is the closest, differing only by $p-1$ versus $p$ in the denominator.
- **Solution 2** ($\pi$) rests on an unsupported claim and is inconsistent with its own $C_6$ discussion.
- **Solution 3** ($p$) is not a time-scale derivation; it confuses graph distance with a revival time.

Since none is correct, the choice below is the least-wrong candidate, not a correct answer.

CHOICE: 1
